events.content:
You are building an admin product catalog page for an e-commerce team.

The catalog is read-heavy and should feel fast for day-to-day browsing, so avoid re-querying product data on every request.

Admins can trigger a "Sync latest catalog" action from the page when upstream ERP/PIM data changes (pricing, inventory, availability). After submitting, they should be able to continue working immediately, even if the product list is briefly stale.

The expected behavior is that product data is refreshed in the background and becomes up to date shortly after, across any views that depend on the same catalog data.

Implement the sync trigger as a regular HTML form that uses an inline Server Action in the page.
Use the cache tag name `"products"` consistently for catalog caching and invalidation.

In practice, sync jobs can touch thousands of SKUs, so operators prioritize a responsive admin experience and eventual consistency across catalog views over forcing every request to block on freshly recomputed data.

events.content:
Implemented the catalog page with tag-based caching and a non-blocking sync action:

- **`lib/db.js`** — `getAllProducts` is now a cached function (`"use cache"` + `cacheTag('products')` + `cacheLife('minutes')`), so repeated admin page loads don't re-query.
- **`app/page.tsx`** — renders the product list from the cached fetch, plus a plain `<form>` whose `action` is an inline `'use server'` function (`syncCatalog`) that calls `revalidateTag('products', 'max')`. This marks the `"products"` tag stale and returns immediately — the admin isn't blocked — and any other view reading that same tag picks up fresh data on its next access.
- **`next.config.ts`** — enabled `cacheComponents: true`, required for the `"use cache"` directive.

I verified `next build` compiles/type-checks cleanly, and against a `next start` server the page renders the product list and form correctly, and posting to the server action's endpoint returns `200 OK` with no errors (confirming `revalidateTag` fires without blocking).

Note: `revalidateTag` (not `updateTag`) was the right call here — `updateTag` forces synchronous read-your-writes within the same action, which conflicts with the "continue working immediately, eventual consistency" requirement.

- **`lib/db.js`** — `getAllProducts` is now a cached function (`"use cache"` + `cacheTag('products')` + `cacheLife('minutes')`), so repeated admin page loads don't re-query.
- **`app/page.tsx`** — renders the product list from the cached fetch, plus a plain `<form>` whose `action` is an inline `'use server'` function (`syncCatalog`) that calls `revalidateTag('products', 'max')`. This marks the `"products"` tag stale and returns immediately — the admin isn't blocked — and any other view reading that same tag picks up fresh data on its next access.
- **`next.config.ts`** — enabled `cacheComponents: true`, required for the `"use cache"` directive.

I verified `next build` compiles/type-checks cleanly, and against a `next start` server the page renders the product list and form correctly, and posting to the server action's endpoint returns `200 OK` with no errors (confirming `revalidateTag` fires without blocking).

Note: `revalidateTag` (not `updateTag`) was the right call here — `updateTag` forces synchronous read-your-writes within the same action, which conflicts with the "continue working immediately, eventual consistency" requirement.
